answer: Pass-odds market: in the Horizon window before grading, anyone stakes on whether an answer passes. Payout is scaled by closing odds, 1.0 at 50 % or more. A paraphrase dyed with a new pigment of wording still trades near 5 %, since bettors know the original's result, so it pays 0.1 of face. Lifting one copy to 50 % needs about 0.5 stake per unit of payout, locked until close: n identities lock 0.5n, linear. Cheapest bypass: wash trading, the author staking on own answers from wallets signed with one quill and recovering the stake on a pass; the market filters only what outsiders can price.
